subject: CS362
filterSummary: Successfully selected 10 videos (5 English, 5 Arabic) covering all topics. For English, selections were dominated by high-reach, high-quality channels like StatQuest and codebasics. For Arabic, selections were also strong, with popular educational channels being chosen. One Arabic topic for Probabilistic Modelling required using the view count exception rule, as no candidates met the standard 3000-view threshold.

coverage.note: All candidates failed the 3000 view count gate; selected the best candidate with >500 views per exception rule.
Only one candidate passed the hard gates.

videos.title: Clustering (4): Gaussian Mixture Models and EM
videos.topic_ar: النمذجة الاحتمالية (الشبكات البايزية ونماذج الخليط الغاوسي)
videos.filter_reason: This is a high-quality, widely-viewed university lecture that clearly explains Gaussian Mixture Models and the EM algorithm, a core and challenging part of this topic.

videos.title: Gradient Boost Part 1 (of 4): Regression Main Ideas
videos.filter_reason: StatQuest provides an exceptionally clear and intuitive explanation of Gradient Boosting, which is often the most confusing part of ensemble learning for students.

videos.title: Machine Learning Tutorial Python - 16: Hyper parameter Tuning (GridSearchCV)
videos.filter_reason: This popular tutorial from codebasics provides a great practical workflow, connecting cross-validation with hyperparameter tuning using GridSearchCV, which directly addresses the student's needs.

videos.title: Yann LeCun - Self-Supervised Learning: The Dark Matter of Intelligence (FAIR Blog Post Explained)
videos.topic_ar: التعلم شبه الخاضع للإشراف والتعلم الذاتي
videos.filter_reason: This highly-viewed video provides an authoritative and deep explanation of a blog post by pioneer Yann LeCun, giving students a strong foundation in self-supervised learning.

videos.title: StatQuest: K-means clustering
videos.topic_ar: التعلم غير الخاضع للإشراف (التجميع وتقليل الأبعاد)
videos.filter_reason: This classic StatQuest video has over 2 million views and provides an unparalleled intuitive explanation of K-means, a fundamental clustering algorithm in unsupervised learning.
